deals.whyRanked: Allegiant lists $69 BOS→FLL on Nov 14 and $52 FLL→BOS on Dec 3 — about $121 round trip, up from $104 as the cheapest Nov 7/12 pairing aged out, still the cheapest verified fare, with the Everglades 50 minutes away.
deals.soloWhy: The free Sun Trolley links the beach and Las Olas without a car, and the lit beachfront promenade stays comfortable for a solo evening walk.

highlights: Shark Valley's flat 15-mile Everglades bike loop
itinerary: Day 1 — Beach promenade at sunset, then Las Olas for dinner.
Day 2 — Everglades Shark Valley tram or bike loop by rental car, evening Riverwalk.
Day 3 — Bonnet House gardens, then a water taxi for lunch before the flight.
guide.gettingAround: The free Sun Trolley covers downtown, Las Olas, and the beach; a rental car is worth it only for the Everglades day trip.
guide.stayArea: The beachfront or Las Olas — both walkable to restaurants, the promenade, and water taxi stops.

deals.whyRanked: Allegiant's page shows $76 BOS→TYS on Oct 31 and $56 TYS→BOS on Nov 7 — about $132 round trip, still second-cheapest, with the Smokies 45 minutes from downtown.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown's compact grid is easy to explore alone on foot, and the Cosby and Greenbrier entrances to the Smokies are a short solo drive with none of the Cades Cove crowds.

highlights: World's Fair Park and the Sunsphere observation deck
Market Square's farmers' stalls and buskers
Ijams Nature Center's quarry swimming hole and trails
South Knoxville's urban wilderness bike/hike loop
Cosby entrance to the Great Smoky Mountains
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, ride the elevator up the Sunsphere for a skyline view, then dinner on Market Square.
Day 2 — Rent a car for the Cosby entrance: the Hen Wallow Falls trail, with a stop at Foothills Parkway overlooks on the drive back.
Day 3 — Morning loop at Ijams Nature Center, then an afternoon at the Knoxville Museum of Art before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown is flat and walkable end to end; a rental car is required to reach any Smokies trailhead.
guide.stayArea: Downtown near Market Square or Gay Street — walkable to restaurants and the Tennessee Theatre.

deals.whyRanked: Momondo shows BOS→DC one-way from $62 (Nov 23) up to ~$121 — a roughly $124–$242 round trip doubled from that range, so the low end is unconfirmed; the Metro and free Smithsonians give DC the best solo score of the three.
deals.soloWhy: Metro reaches nearly everything, the 19 free Smithsonian museums fill days at no cost, and Kayak/OpenTable ranked DC a top US solo destination.

highlights: National Mall monument walk at dusk
Air & Space and African American History museums
Georgetown waterfront and C&O Canal towpath
itinerary: Day 1 — Lincoln Memorial to the Capitol along the Mall, dinner on U Street.
Day 2 — Smithsonian morning (reserve NMAAHC timed pass), afternoon at Georgetown and the C&O towpath.
Day 3 — Great Falls Park by rideshare or Old Town Alexandria by Metro before the flight.
guide.gettingAround: Metro and walking cover everything; DCA is on the Yellow/Blue lines, so no car is needed.
guide.stayArea: Dupont Circle — walkable, on the Red Line, with plenty of hostels and mid-priced hotels.
